aviso: This information is for guidance only and has no legal validity. For support, deadlines and procedures, always check the linked official source before applying.
criterio: When Spanish support, a deadline, a right or a service is mentioned, its source is given. Practical recommendations are presented as supports, not as clinical treatment. A specific adaptation depends on the person and the context; a diagnosis on its own does not automatically grant all the measures described.

fichas.title: Flying with a non-visible disability
fichas.lede: Aena has its own badge for people with non-visible disabilities. It is free, requested through its website and helps staff identify that a person may need more time, understanding or support while moving through the airport.

p: As of 1 September 2026, Aena lists 20 airports where the badge can be used. Showing it can give access to the security lane dedicated to families and people with reduced mobility where the airport has one; if that lane does not exist, Aena says it will facilitate, as far as possible, passage through the general security control.

The badge is not fast track, does not include accompaniment and does not exempt anyone from security checks or procedures. If travelling as a family, it is enough for one member to carry it. It can be carried printed or in digital format.

The Sin Barreras assistance service (PMR) is a different service, designed for people who need assistance during the airport journey. It is advisable to request it in advance through the airline or through Aena.

The sunflower lanyard is a private international initiative. Aena explains that it can indicate that a person needs more help or time, but it does not give access to the dedicated security control. For Aena’s specific benefits, the Aena badge must be requested.

Download the badge, review the airport map, locate quiet rooms if there are any, keep the boarding pass and documents in one place and anticipate the steps of the journey in writing. Aena offers support materials to prepare the route.

fichas.title: Public transport and getting around
fichas.lede: Moving around the city combines timetables, orientation, noise, crowds, platform changes, tickets and quick decisions. The barrier may be in one part of the journey, not in “using transport” in general.

p: Prepare the route with a clear starting point and end point, save a screenshot of the journey, identify an alternative if the service is cancelled and carry enough battery. For someone who needs it, a visual sequence of five or six steps may be more useful than a long explanation.

Accessible information, help locating a stop or platform, time to understand an instruction and reasonable access measures where there is a disability. Ley 15/2022 expressly includes transport among the areas protected against discrimination.

sections.h: If travelling alone is not yet safe
p: Practise one section at a time: first accompanied, then with agreed follow-up and finally independently if the person wants to and can. Autonomy does not mean withdrawing support too soon.

fichas.title: Shopping, errands and waiting
fichas.lede: Shopping brings together a list, money, decisions, travel, searching, lights, noise, interaction and changes when a product is unavailable. Separating those steps helps identify what support is needed.

p: A short list ordered by area, a visible budget, a photo of the product if the brand or format matters, and a plan for substitutions: “if there is no A, I buy B; if there is no B either, I do not buy anything”.

Go at a less crowded time, use self-checkout if it makes interaction easier, carry headphones or glasses if they help, and split a large shop into two. Online shopping can be functional support, not a “failure” of autonomy.

Establishments open to the public are subject to accessibility and non-discrimination obligations. Information can be requested in an understandable format, along with reasonable and proportionate adjustments.

fichas.title: Restaurants and eating out
fichas.lede: Eating out adds smell, conversation, waiting, an unfamiliar menu, social rules and a lack of control over preparation. The difficulty does not depend only on “being selective”.

p: Look at the menu and photos, ask about ingredients or cross-contamination when clinically relevant, book a quiet table and choose less busy times. If the person needs a safe food, check the venue’s policy beforehand.
Ask for components separately, remove sauces or side dishes, request a simple explanation of the dish and allow the person to stop eating without turning it into a public negotiation.

The regulations on goods and services require accessibility and non-discrimination for people with disabilities, but they do not oblige a restaurant to prepare any imaginable dish. The request must be specific and viable; for allergies or coeliac disease, the relevant food-safety rules should also be followed.

fichas.title: Cinema, theatre and museums with fewer stimuli
fichas.lede: Relaxed screenings and low-stimulation visits reduce some barriers related to noise, light, waiting and rules about staying in place. They are not exclusive to autism: they may be useful for hyperacusis, misophonia, anxiety, APD, sensory overload or other needs.

p: In Spain there are cinemas, theatres, museums and cultural centres that schedule relaxed sessions or lower-stimulation time slots. Common measures include keeping some light on, reducing volume, removing trailers or unnecessary effects, allowing people to enter and leave, and offering advance information about the space.
The offer changes by city and programme, so it is advisable to check directly with the venue before travelling.

Advance information about duration, lights, sounds, queues and rules; a location near an exit; the possibility of waiting outside the queue; permission to use hearing protection; and an alternative if a specific activity is not accessible. Where there is a disability, the regulations on accessibility of goods and services strengthen the obligation to provide accessible information and reasonable, proportionate measures.

A brief message works better than explaining the whole clinical history: “I need to know whether there will be strobe lights, high volume or long queues, and whether it is possible to enter/leave during the activity”.

sources.label: Real Decreto 193/2023 · accessibility of goods and services

fichas.title: Physical activity, sport and swimming
fichas.lede: Physical activity can be walking, dancing, swimming, cycling, training, playing or moving in whatever way is possible for the person. There is no sport “for neurodivergent people”: what matters is that the activity is accessible, safe and chosen.

p: A small group if needed; clear instructions; visual demonstration; the same structure between sessions; a prior visit; breaks; adaptations for noise, clothing or physical contact; and the option of an individual activity if the team format creates a barrier.

Ask about quiet lanes or time slots, temperature, swimming-cap rules, hairdryer noise and changing-room rules. For some people, the hardest part is not swimming, but entering the changing room, waiting, showering or getting out of the water.

Where there is a disability, accessibility and non-discrimination also apply to goods, services and sporting activities open to the public. This does not guarantee every imaginable adjustment, but it does require reasonable and proportionate measures to be considered.

fichas.title: Leisure, art, music, animals and nature
fichas.lede: Leisure does not need to be therapeutic. It can be rest, interest, creation, movement or connection with other people.

p: Offer activities because the person enjoys them, not because they “work on skills”. An intense interest can be a route to belonging and learning without having to become a profession.
Flexible duration, queue-free entry where that option exists, headphones, advance information, space to withdraw, a companion and the possibility of taking part partially.

Distinguish living with animals, assisted activities and assistance dogs. A companion animal can contribute to wellbeing, but that does not give it the access rights reserved for accredited assistance dogs.

fichas.title: Assistance dogs: what the law recognises
fichas.lede: Real Decreto 409/2025 establishes a national framework on the activity and welfare of assistance dogs and recognises several categories, including dogs for autistic people. Specific recognition and accreditation are also coordinated with regional regulations.

p: The royal decree regulates basic requirements, training, identification, welfare and access to the environment. The category of assistance dog is not obtained simply by buying or training a companion dog independently: there is a procedure, and entities or professionals must meet requirements.

Define the specific tasks the dog is expected to perform, who will take on its daily care, costs, waiting times, living together, travel and what will happen when the dog ages. For minors, the family has a central role in handling and welfare.

The national framework protects access for the assistance-dog partnership to many spaces and services, without prejudice to regional details. It is advisable to check the accreditation required in the region where the person lives.

fichas.title: If a vulnerable person goes missing: what to prepare and what to do
fichas.lede: In a concerning disappearance, there is no need to wait 24 hours. The response must be adapted to the age, health, communication, autonomy and circumstances of the missing person.

p: Recent photo, physical description, important medication, communication method, usual places, contacts, vehicle registration or transport if relevant, and any information that could guide the search. Update it when the photo or information changes.

Call 112 if there is immediate risk and report the disappearance without delay to the National Police or Guardia Civil. Bring the photo and available information. Do not delay the report because of the idea that 24 hours must pass.

AlertCops allows chat with the Police/Guardia Civil, an SOS button and location sharing with contacts; some “Guardian” functions are activated for specific services or circumstances. It does not replace reporting the disappearance and should not be presented as a permanent location system for another person without their knowledge.

sources.label: CNDES · Publications: II Strategic Plan and annual reports
CNDES · II Strategic Plan on Missing Persons (2026–2029), accessible PDF

fichas.notaFuente: The II Strategic Plan on Missing Persons is in force from 2026 to 2029, with 5.1 million in funding, five lines of action, thirteen objectives and 102 measures.

fichas.title: School and secondary school: support, adaptations, attendance and exams
fichas.lede: The LOE/LOMLOE requires specific educational support needs to be identified, resources to be provided and inclusion and non-discrimination to be ensured. Specific supports are also regulated by each autonomous community.

p: Access adaptations, communication supports, changes of location, breaks, anticipation, technology, accessible material, assessment adjustments, guidance-team intervention and individualised measures. The law covers needs related to disability, language and communication disorders, attention or learning, high abilities and other circumstances.

Request a meeting with the tutor/guidance team and state the barrier: “in written exams they do not finish because of reading speed”, “the dining room triggers overload”, “they cannot answer orally in this situation”. Ask what measure is agreed, who applies it and when it will be reviewed.

Persistent attendance difficulties need investigation into what is happening: anxiety, bullying, overload, pain, sleep, learning, transport or conflict. Punishing absence without identifying the barrier can make it worse.

fichas.title: The Ministry grant for educational support (NEAE)
fichas.lede: It is the annual national call for grants and subsidies for students with specific educational support needs. It should always be published with the school year, deadline and amounts for that year.

p: The application period is open from 19 May 2026 at 08:00 to 10 September 2026 at 15:00. The application is submitted through the Ministry’s electronic office. The Ministry reminds applicants that these grants are incompatible with the general grant for post-compulsory studies.

The call includes different cases of specific need and programmes for high abilities. The exact requirements on disability, age, reports, income and type of support must be checked in the call for that school year; it is not advisable to reuse the previous year’s requirements automatically.

The report must relate to the support requested. Before submitting, check that the documents specifically evidence the need for which transport, dining, re-education or another item is being requested.

sources.label: Ministerio de Educación, FP y Deportes · Catalogue entry: grant for specific educational support needs
Ministerio de Educación, FP y Deportes · Call for the 2026–2027 school year

fichas.title: Studying at university with support
fichas.lede: Spanish universities have support services or units for students with disabilities and accessibility needs. Specific adaptations depend on the evidenced need and on each university’s regulations and procedures.

p: The Fundación ONCE University Guide makes it possible to locate, university by university, support services, accessibility resources, assistive products and adaptations in learning and assessment.

Measures may include extra time, accessible formats, room changes, technological supports, adjustments in placements and coordination with teaching staff. There is no identical, automatic adaptation for everyone with the same diagnosis.

Contact the support service before classes begin or as soon as the need appears. It is advisable to provide the available report or certificate and, above all, to explain the specific barrier: reading, writing, noise, attendance, time, communication, mobility or assessment.
Ask for the response in writing and use the university’s internal review or complaint procedures. Equal treatment and accessibility also apply to education.

sources.label: Ley General de derechos de las personas con discapacidad

fichas.title: Looking for work as a neurodivergent person
fichas.lede: Looking for work may require different supports from those needed once someone has been hired. This sheet brings together entry points and reminds readers that disclosing a diagnosis in a recruitment process is not a general obligation.

p: In Spain there are guidance and job-matching services specialised in disability and neurodivergence, as well as public employment services. Inserta Empleo (Fundación ONCE) works with people with recognised disabilities; autism organisations and specialised programmes also offer training, guidance and contact with companies.

A readable CV, a brief explanation of strengths and tasks done well, specific examples of experience and a private list of adjustments that might be useful. There is no need to turn the interview into a clinical explanation.

Some employment measures and specific quotas require a recognised disability degree of 33% or higher. Other ordinary job offers do not. It is advisable to check each programme’s requirement and not assume that “neurodivergent” and “recognised disability” are administratively equivalent.

sources.label: Ley General de derechos de las personas con discapacidad

fichas.title: Reasonable adjustments at work
fichas.lede: Once someone has been hired, the problem is no longer “how to get a job”, but what changes make it possible to perform the role without an avoidable disadvantage.

p: Article 40 of RDL 1/2013 requires companies to adopt appropriate measures to adapt the workplace and ensure accessibility for people with disabilities, unless they impose an excessive burden.

Written instructions; fewer interruptions; headphones where compatible with safety; a quieter location; reasonable changes to working hours; remote working where the role and agreement allow it; a priority agenda; time for training; adjustments in interviews or tests.

Describe the barrier, the proposed measure and how it makes it possible to do the work. There is no need to provide more clinical information than necessary. Keep the request and the response in writing.

fichas.title: Getting a driving licence as a neurodivergent person
fichas.lede: The DGT maintains accessibility measures for people with specific learning difficulties and disabilities. The current guide available on its website is the 3rd edition, October 2024.

p: The DGT recommends supports for the theory and practical tests: clear and concise instructions, consideration of orientation or right/left difficulties, sufficient anticipation of manoeuvres and measures to reduce reading and processing barriers. Specific application is coordinated with the Jefatura and the examining centre.

The driver assessment centre assesses aptitudes under the General Driver Regulations. A diagnosis alone cannot automatically imply “fit” or “unfit”; functioning, required reports and specific conditions matter.

Give notice of the need for adaptation in good time and bring the supporting documentation indicated by the DGT. Do not wait until the day of the test to explain a barrier that requires prior organisation.

fichas.avisoFuente: The DGT guide is in its 3rd edition, from October 2024. The edition number is in the PDF path: when a new one is released, it must be changed.

fichas.title: Going to the doctor, the dentist or the emergency room
fichas.lede: A healthcare appointment can be made more accessible when what is going to happen is anticipated and the load of waiting, communication and stimuli is reduced. The person has the right to receive understandable information and, if they have a disability, to the support needed to take part in their healthcare decisions.

p: The first or last appointment of the day; written instructions; warning before touch; a step-by-step explanation; more time to answer; help from a trusted person if requested; reduced waiting; a less noisy space; and use of the person’s communication method.
Ley 41/2002 establishes that, if the patient is a person with a disability, support measures and information in suitable formats will be offered to help them give consent themselves.

A one-page sheet with medication, allergies, communication method, signs of pain, what helps and what worsens the situation. If the person uses AAC, bring it charged and available: it must not be taken away because “today it is time to talk to the doctor”.
Clinical safety comes first. Even so, triage can be told what communication or sensory barriers may make examination difficult and what simple adjustments can make it easier.

concepts: Other specified feeding or eating disorders (OSFED)

fichas.title: Hospital stays, tests and medical procedures
fichas.lede: A hospital stay adds changing staff, fasting, pain, alarms and loss of control over routine. Preparing communication and consent reduces risks, not just distress.

p: Ask for written information: where to go, how long it lasts, fasting, clothing, companion, sedation and what will happen afterwards. Prepare a communication sheet and ask what objects or supports can come in.

Ley 41/2002 requires free and voluntary consent after receiving information; for people with disabilities, support and accessible formats must be offered so that the person themselves can participate and consent.
Keep AAC available, explain before touching, reduce changes of professional where possible, group procedures if clinically viable and record which signs indicate pain or deterioration in that person.

fichas.title: Anxiety, panic and mental health crises: what to do and where to ask for help
fichas.lede: An intense crisis first needs safety and reduced demand. Not all anxiety is an emergency, and not every emergency can be resolved with breathing techniques.

p: Reduce questions, offer a safer or less stimulating place, speak in short sentences and avoid debating whether there are “reasons” to feel afraid. If the person knows a strategy that helps, make it easier; do not impose physical contact.

Record triggers, duration, physical symptoms and what helped. If it repeats, limits life or changes form, request professional assessment to distinguish anxiety, panic, medication effects, physical problems or other conditions.
In Spain, 024 is free, confidential and available 24/7 for people with suicidal thoughts or behaviour and for those close to them. In an immediate life-threatening emergency, call 112.

sources.label: NICE · Panic disorder and GAD CG113

fichas.title: Pain, gastrointestinal health and body signals
fichas.lede: Abdominal pain, constipation, reflux, headache or musculoskeletal pain are assessed and treated even if the person communicates discomfort in an unusual way.

p: A change in sleep, irritability, food refusal, repetitive movement or loss of skills may accompany pain. If the person has difficulty identifying or expressing sensations, ask with concrete options and observe changes from their usual pattern.
Time, location, intensity with a scale the person understands, food, bowel movements, menstruation, medication, activity and what improves or worsens it. Take the record to the professional.

Sudden intense pain, dehydration, bleeding, breathing difficulty, significant altered consciousness or other warning signs require urgent care. Neurodivergence must not be used to explain a physical symptom without examining it.

concepts: Other specified feeding or eating disorders (OSFED)

fichas.title: Epilepsy and other recurrent seizures: what to prepare
fichas.lede: When a person has epilepsy or another condition with recurrent episodes, the people who live or work with them need a simple, up-to-date plan.

p: How seizures usually begin, usual duration, rescue medication if prescribed, when to administer it, when to call 112, contacts and what to do afterwards. It must reflect the healthcare team’s instructions, not generic instructions from the internet.

Agree who keeps the medication, who knows how to administer it, how privacy is protected and how substitutes or new staff are informed. Do not prevent activities by default: assess the risk of each specific activity.

Note duration and characteristics. If it is the first seizure, lasts longer than stated in the plan, repeats without recovery, or there is injury/breathing difficulty, activate urgent care according to health instructions.

fichas.title: Menstruation, menopause and sexual health
fichas.lede: Hormonal changes can alter pain, sleep, temperature, energy, mood and sensory tolerance. Not every change should be attributed to neurodivergence.

p: Prepare products in several places, try textures and formats, use reminders if anticipating the change is difficult, and record pain or bleeding. If menstrual hygiene is difficult, practise the sequence outside the urgent moment.
Record cycle changes, hot flushes, sleep, mood and functioning. Take specific information to primary care or gynaecology. Symptoms may require assessment and individualised treatment options.
Information and consent must be understandable and respect privacy and autonomy. Gender identity must not be used to deny care related to organs or bodily functions the person has.

fichas.title: ARFID, eating disorders and pica: when everyday support needs clinical care
fichas.lede: Food selectivity, ARFID, anorexia, bulimia, binge-eating disorder, OSFED and pica are not the same. Sharing a difficulty with food does not allow the same treatment to be assumed.

p: Weight loss or altered growth, fainting, signs of dehydration or deficiencies, dependence on supplements or enteral nutrition, binge eating, vomiting or compensatory behaviours, intense fear related to weight/body shape, or repeated ingestion of non-food substances.

sections.h: What to take to the appointment
p: A real record of food and drinks, supplements, gastrointestinal symptoms, growth if available, reason for refusal and differences between home and other contexts. Do not “improve” the record to make it look like a more varied diet.
Nutritional safety comes first. Avoid turning every meal into an improvised exposure or a power struggle. The specific approach depends on the diagnosis and medical status.

concepts: Other specified feeding or eating disorders (OSFED)

fichas.title: Communication without speech, mutism, apraxia, stuttering and difficult speech
fichas.lede: Not speaking, speaking little, stuttering or being unable to speak in a specific situation are different experiences. The common rule is not to confuse availability of speech with understanding or capacity to decide.

p: Give time, ask one question at a time, allow writing or pointing, do not automatically finish the sentences of someone who stutters, and do not require oral speech to prove understanding.

Agree an alternative way to respond before the blocking situation appears: tablet, keyboard, cards, gestures, board or support person. AAC must be available even if the person also speaks at other times.
Reduce pressure and allow non-oral responses. Rewarding, punishing or putting the person at the centre so that they “finally speak” increases demand and can worsen anxiety.

fichas.title: Sensory overload, hyperacusis, misophonia and auditory processing
fichas.lede: Noise, light, smell, touch and movement can be difficult for different reasons. Hyperacusis, misophonia, APD and sensory overload are not synonyms, although some everyday adaptations may overlap.

p: Headphones or protectors when safe, breaks outside the environment, seating away from loudspeakers, advance information about alarms or lights, shopping at quiet times and the possibility of turning off unnecessary stimuli.

sections.h: Do not use protection all day by default
p: Constant hearing protection may not be appropriate for everyone and may hinder communication or safety. In hyperacusis, APD or new symptoms, audiology/ENT assessment is advisable depending on the case.

Describe the stimulus and the solution: “I need a seat away from the loudspeaker” is more useful than “I have sensory sensitivity”. In services open to the public, reasonable measures can be part of accessibility.

fichas.title: Interoception, proprioception and the vestibular system in everyday life
fichas.lede: Hunger, thirst, pain, needing the toilet, body position and balance depend on different systems. There is no single “sensory alteration” that explains everything.

p: Reminders for water, food and the toilet; clothing suited to the temperature even if the sensation arrives late; visual cues; movement breaks; and balance supports when indicated by a professional.
Not noticing thirst, pain or the need to use the toilet can have physical consequences. A functional reminder is an adaptation, not training to “feel correctly”.

If there is dizziness, falls, loss of balance, unidentified pain or new changes, look for medical causes. Vestibular or proprioceptive exercises should not be prescribed generically without a specific need.

fichas.title: Emotional regulation, rumination, rejection, guilt and perfectionism
fichas.lede: Regulating an emotion does not mean no longer feeling it. The everyday aim is to recognise what is happening, reduce harm and recover the ability to decide.

p: Lower demands, reduce language, separate the person from the situation if they want that, postpone important decisions and avoid requiring a full explanation during the emotional peak.

Review what happened beforehand, what interpretation appeared and what consequences it had. In rumination or perfectionism, limiting endless review with “good enough” criteria may be more useful than seeking total certainty.

If guilt, fear of rejection, anger, rumination or shame persistently limit life, are accompanied by self-harm or suicide risk, or appear alongside depression, OCD or anxiety, they need specific assessment.

sources.label: NICE · Common mental health problems CG123

fichas.title: Sleep: what to observe and where to start
fichas.lede: Sleeping badly is not one single thing. It may be difficult to fall asleep, stay asleep, waking may happen too early, or the person may sleep enough hours without feeling rested. The cause and support change according to the pattern.

p: Record one or two weeks: bedtime, how long it takes to fall asleep, awakenings, final wake-up time, naps, medication, caffeine, pain, activity and how the person functions the next day. That record helps distinguish an irregular schedule from a persistent problem.

Sufficiently regular times, a clear contrast between day and night, light and activity during the day, a transition routine to bed and reducing stimuli that keep the person alert. If there is chronic insomnia, a sleep-specific behavioural intervention has more support than limiting it to “sleep hygiene”.

The Spanish consensus published in 2026 recommends starting with assessment, a sleep diary and personalised non-pharmacological measures. The pharmacological step belongs to the professional and requires follow-up and reassessment; the website sheet must not turn doses from a clinical consensus into self-medication instructions.

sources.label: Spanish 2026 consensus on insomnia in autistic minors

fichas.title: Food, explained through the senses
fichas.lede: Texture, smell, temperature, chewing sound, mixing foods and predictability can completely change the experience of eating. Sensory selectivity does not automatically mean ARFID or another eating disorder.

p: Rejection of mixed or lumpy textures; preference for specific brands, shapes or temperatures; rejection because of smell before tasting; difficulty eating in new places; and a need for foods not to touch.

First record what is eaten; keep safe foods; make changes one at a time; present the new food alongside the familiar one; avoid deception or hidden mixtures; and separate the nutritional aim from the aim of “eating like everyone else”.

sections.h: When to move to the clinical sheet
p: If there is weight loss or altered growth, signs of deficiencies, dependence on supplements or enteral feeding, binge eating, compensatory behaviours, ingestion of non-food substances or severe interference with life, ARFID, eating disorders, pica or other medical causes must be assessed.

fichas.title: Hygiene and self-care
fichas.lede: Showering, brushing teeth, cutting nails, caring for hair or changing clothes are sequences involving touch, temperature, smell, balance, time and planning. Support should target the difficult step, not judge willingness.

p: Is it hard to start, tolerate the water, bear the brush, remember all the steps, enter the bathroom or finish? Changing everything at once makes it impossible to know what works.

Visual sequence; fragrance-free products; towel prepared; timer; electric or manual toothbrush according to tolerance; shower seat if needed; cutting nails in several rounds; clothes organised in outfits; and choosing the time of day with the most energy.

Autonomy includes taking part in decisions about one’s own body and accepting help when it is needed. If there is dependency for basic activities of daily living, Ley 39/2006 provides for support within the autonomy and dependency system.

fichas.title: Cooking and home safety
fichas.lede: Cooking combines planning, working memory, coordination, heat, knives, smells and time control. A person may be able to prepare some meals safely and need support with others.

p: Keep frequent utensils visible, use recipes with numbered steps, gather ingredients before turning on the hob and reduce decisions. “Assembly” meals without cooking also count as cooking for everyday life.

Visible timers, hobs with automatic switch-off if possible, handles turned inwards, suitable gloves and a clear rule for which tasks require another person. If there is epilepsy, fainting, motor difficulties or altered risk judgement, adapt the type of cooking.
Practise one recipe until it becomes automatic before adding another. The aim is sufficiently safe and sustainable eating, not mastering complex culinary techniques.

fichas.title: Organisation, planning, executive functions and daily tasks
fichas.lede: Knowing what needs to be done does not guarantee being able to start it, order it and finish it. Working memory, time estimation, transitions between tasks and emotional load can block simple actions.

p: Turn “tidy the room” into observable actions; leave the next object prepared; use short lists; a “pending” tray; calendars with few categories; and alarms that say what to do, not only that “an alarm has gone off”.

Reduce the first step until it is executable: open the document, put the clothes next to the washing machine, take out a frying pan. For some people it works to start alongside another person —in person or remotely—even if each person is doing their own task.
If an organisation system requires maintaining ten apps, colour codes and daily reviews, it can become another task. The best system is the one that still works in a difficult week.

sources.label: Ley General de discapacidad · reasonable adjustments

fichas.title: Rest, fatigue, masking and recovery
fichas.lede: Resting is not only sleeping. It can also mean reducing conversation, decisions, light, journeys, emotional labour or the need to appear a certain way. Recovery needs real demand to be lowered.

sections.h: Signs that rest is not reaching far enough
p: It becomes increasingly hard to start tasks, tolerate noise, speak, eat, decide or maintain routines that used to be possible. There is no need to wait for a crisis to reorganise the load.
Blocks without interaction, days with fewer transitions, simple meals, automating tasks, working from a less stimulating space when possible and reserving recovery time after high-demand activities.

The term has a growing literature but no validated diagnostic criteria. If exhaustion is intense or prolonged, depression, anaemia, pain, sleep, medication and other medical causes must also be reviewed; calling everything “burnout” can hide them.

fichas.title: Housing, living together, autonomy and support at home
fichas.lede: A home can be inaccessible because of noise, layout, transport, cohabitation or the tasks required to maintain it. “Living independently” can include daily support.

p: Indoor and outdoor noise, lighting, neighbours, transport, stairs, safety, the possibility of having a personal space, visible storage, total cost and proximity to support. The cheapest housing can be unviable if it creates a huge travel load.

Home help, personal assistance, support with cleaning, meals, shopping or financial management, home automation and supported housing depending on the situation. The dependency system seeks to make autonomous existence in the usual environment easier where possible.
Agree in writing on tasks, noise, visits, use of shared areas and what happens when someone needs to be alone. A useful household rule describes behaviours, not personal traits.

fichas.title: Respite care: what it is and how to ask for it
fichas.lede: Respite care offers hours, activities or stays that allow those providing intensive support to rest or reconcile care with other responsibilities. It is not “abandoning care”: it is a possible part of a sustainable support network.

p: Common forms include hourly support at home or in the community, supported leisure, weekends and short stays. Availability depends on the autonomous community, organisation and annual funding.
Ask at the local organisation’s Family Support Service, municipal social services or regional network. It is advisable to do this in advance because holiday and weekend places often close early.
Profile of people admitted, staff ratio and training, health support if needed, transport, cost, medication policy, communication during the stay and what happens if the person needs to return early.

fichas.title: Family: changes, siblings, motherhood/fatherhood and work-life balance
fichas.lede: A move, separation, birth, illness or change of carer alters routines and relationships at the same time. Each family member may need different information and support.

p: Say what changes, what stays the same and when it will happen. Use a calendar or photos if they help. Do not promise that “everything will stay the same” if it is not true.

Do not turn a sibling into the default carer. They can collaborate like any family member, but they need their own time, information suited to their age and the right to express anger or tiredness without feeling guilty.
Simplify logistics, share calendars, automate shopping, accept outside support and reserve recovery time. A parent’s need for support does not invalidate their capacity to parent.

fichas.title: Free communication tools and pictograms
fichas.lede: Augmentative and alternative communication includes many tools: boards, pictograms, text, keyboards, signs, synthesised speech and devices. Pictograms are one option, not the compulsory system for everyone.

p: ARASAAC offers pictograms and materials for communication and cognitive accessibility. There are also communicators and digital schedules that can include images, photographs, text and voice. The tool must fit the person’s motor access, vision, reading, language and preferences.

A person who uses AAC needs access to their system throughout the day, including at school, in hospital, during leisure and in stressful situations. Taking the device away because it “distracts” is equivalent to removing a communication route.

ARASAAC resources are distributed under a CC BY-NC-SA licence, and the terms of use exclude commercial use without authorisation. That is why free downloads and commercial materials should be clearly separated.

fichas.title: Legal support when turning 18
fichas.lede: Since the reform introduced by Ley 8/2021, an adult person retains legal capacity. When they need help to exercise it, the system is based on support and on respecting their will, wishes and preferences.

p: De facto guardianship can cover everyday support without a formal court measure; voluntary measures allow the person themselves to arrange before a notary who they want to support them and how; and curatorship is a judicial support measure, usually assistive, with representation reserved for specific exceptional cases.

A measure is not chosen solely by diagnosis. It is necessary to look at which decisions the person can make alone, which they can make with accessible information, which require accompaniment and whether there are conflicts of interest.

Check the effect on benefits, tax advantages, banks and procedures that are already being carried out. For an individual decision, it is advisable to use a specialised legal service; this sheet is for guidance.

fichas.title: Finding an association by condition and community
fichas.lede: Not all 185 concepts have their own federation. Where an associative network exists, the national organisation is usually the best entry point for locating regional or provincial associations and finding out what services are available.

p: Start with the national federation or confederation and check its list of member organisations. For autism: Confederación Autismo España and FESPAU; for intellectual and developmental disability: Plena inclusión; for other conditions it is advisable to look for the relevant national federation and verify that the organisation keeps its activity and contact details up to date.

Guidance on procedures, support groups, leisure, respite, employment, training, family accompaniment or referral to local resources. Each organisation has different criteria, funding and waiting lists.

The website links to organisations and sources; it does not certify treatments or turn an association into a clinical authority. Each entry should indicate geographical scope and the date the link was checked.

fichas.title: Bullying, discrimination, racism and how to act
fichas.lede: Bullying and discrimination are not “social skills problems” of the person receiving them. The person must be protected, the facts recorded and the appropriate channel for the context used.

p: Date, place, what happened, people present, screenshots or messages and who was informed. Describing concrete behaviours prevents the case from being reduced to “they do not get along”.

At school: the coexistence/bullying protocol and the school leadership. At work: the company, prevention/human resources, workers’ representation or labour inspectorate depending on the case. In services open to the public: complaint and, if appropriate, administrative or judicial route. If there is a threat or crime, Police/Guardia Civil.

Ley 15/2022 protects against discrimination in employment, education, healthcare, transport, culture, housing, goods and services, the internet and other areas. Disability also has specific protection under RDL 1/2013.

fichas.title: Money, contracts, forms and paperwork
fichas.lede: Managing money and administration combines dates, reading, calculation, memory, passwords and decisions. Help can be occasional without removing autonomy over decisions.

p: Set up direct debits for stable payments, limit the number of accounts, activate alerts, separate money for fixed and variable expenses and keep contracts in a single folder. For paperwork, a list of “documents they always ask for” avoids starting from zero.
People with disabilities have the right to accessibility conditions and, in goods and services, to information in suitable formats and reasonable, proportionate measures.

Distinguish support from substitution: reading a letter, explaining options or accompanying someone to an appointment does not mean deciding for the person. If stable legal supports are needed, link to the sheet on support when turning 18.

fichas.title: Abuse, exploitation and safe relationships
fichas.lede: Dependence on support, isolation, communication difficulties or difficulty interpreting intentions may increase vulnerabilities, but responsibility always lies with the person who abuses or exploits.

p: Someone controls money or documents, forces secrets to be kept, threatens to withdraw care, pressures for images to be sent, uses the diagnosis to discredit, prevents the person from seeing others or forces physical/sexual contact.

Prioritise a safe place, alert a trusted person and preserve evidence when doing so does not increase risk. In an emergency, call 112. If it is violence against a woman, 016 offers information, legal advice and psychosocial support; also by WhatsApp on 600 000 016.
Explanations about reporting, resources and protective measures must be adapted to the person’s form of communication and understanding. Do not remove their voice because they need support.

fichas.title: Online safety, privacy, outing and cyberbullying
fichas.lede: Digital safety includes passwords, images, location, scams, sexual pressure, outing, harassment and relationships that begin or continue online.

p: Unique passwords with a password manager, two-factor authentication where available, and reviewing who can see location and stories. Do not share verification codes even if the person asking for them seems familiar.

Save screenshots and links, block when safe, use the platform’s reporting tools and ask for help. INCIBE offers 017, free and confidential, from 8:00 to 23:00 every day, with technical, legal and psychosocial advice.

The AEPD has a Youth Channel for questions about minors’ privacy and data protection. Sharing images or sensitive information can have serious consequences even if the person who initially shared it had legitimate access.

fichas.title: LGBTI+ and neurodiversity: name, pronouns, identity and respectful care
fichas.lede: Being neurodivergent does not invalidate a gender identity or orientation. They are different dimensions and neither automatically “explains” the other.

p: Use the name and pronouns the person indicates, do not disclose their identity to third parties without permission, and do not turn a consultation about health, school or work into an interrogation about identity when it is not relevant.

Ley 4/2023 establishes measures against LGBTI discrimination and principles of healthcare for trans people based on non-pathologisation, autonomy, informed consent, privacy and non-discrimination. It also provides for educational protocols to support trans students and address transphobic bullying.
Record the facts and use the channel of the school, company, health service or administration. Ley 15/2022 also provides a general framework for equal treatment in multiple areas.

fichas.title: Late diagnosis, self-acceptance, self-advocacy and how to ask for support
fichas.lede: Receiving a diagnostic explanation or identifying with an experience can reorganise years of personal history. The practical part begins by translating that information into concrete needs.

p: It is not necessary to change every routine or tell everyone. Review one situation at a time: work, home, study, health, relationships. Ask: “what is hard for me and what changes if I modify the environment?”
Use a brief formula: barrier + impact + adjustment. Example: “In long meetings I lose information when several people speak; I need an agenda in advance and agreements in writing”.

Defending needs does not mean doing everything alone. Someone can be brought to a meeting, a written response can be requested, AAC can be used or accessible information can be requested. Disability legislation recognises reasonable adjustments and accessibility where applicable.

fichas.title: Disability, dependency, poverty and access to support
fichas.lede: Diagnosis, degree of disability and dependency status are different administrative things. A person may have a clinical condition and not have a recognised disability percentage or dependency degree.

p: Disability: recognition of degree and access to certain rights/measures. Dependency: assessment of the need for help with activities of daily living and an individual care plan. Social services: municipal or regional resources that may depend on income, household situation or other criteria.

Recent reports, a description of real functioning, support the family already provides, relevant expenses and identity/residence documents. Do not limit the file to the name of the diagnosis: explain which tasks require help and how often.

Lack of money can prevent transport, suitable housing, therapies, food or rest. It must not be presented as a personal trait. The search for support has to include general benefits, not only those labelled “disability”.

fichas.title: Friendship, loneliness, belonging and social fatigue
fichas.lede: Having few relationships is not the same as being lonely. The useful question is whether the amount and type of connection match what the person wants and can sustain.

p: Agree frequency of messages, accept short plans, meet around a shared interest, allow silences and do not automatically interpret taking time to reply as lack of interest.
Schedule recovery after events, reduce chains of commitments and choose less demanding formats: walking together, playing, watching a film or sharing an activity without continuous conversation.

If the person wants more connection, look for spaces where the activity has structure and shared interests. The aim is not to increase the number of contacts, but to find relationships that are sufficiently safe and reciprocal.

sources.label: WHO · Social connection: questions and answers
WHO · Commission on Social Connection, report “From loneliness to social connection” (2025)

fichas.title: Relationships, conflict, boundaries and consent
fichas.lede: A safe relationship needs the ability to say yes, no, not yet, I need time and I have changed my mind. Boundaries are not deduced from diagnosis or from how long someone has been in a relationship.

p: Talk about time alone, messages, money, visits, physical contact, sex, household tasks and how to ask for a pause. If a rule exists only in one person’s head, it is easy to turn a misunderstanding into an accusation.
It must be free and can be withdrawn. Freezing, not responding or giving in out of fear is not the same as clear consent. Communication can be oral, written, signed or through AAC.

Arguing is not the same as abuse. But threats, control of money or contacts, isolation, sexual coercion, fear or constant surveillance require leaving the frame of “improving communication” and moving to safety and specialised support.

fichas.title: Sexuality and accessible sex education
fichas.lede: Accessible sex education includes the body, puberty, consent, privacy, contraception, infections, orientation, identity, pleasure and relationships. It is not limited to preventing risks.

p: Direct language, clear names for body parts, concrete examples, visual materials if they help, and repeating information at different stages. Separate public/private rules from ideas of shame.

Teach both how to say no and how to recognise another person’s no; practise how to ask for help; explain that a relationship, gift or date does not create a sexual debt. Include digital safety and intimate images.

The person must receive understandable information and take part in decisions. Identity or orientation are not diagnoses; when sexual or reproductive healthcare is needed, the approach must be respectful, confidential and non-discriminatory.
